title: SessionRunParams
description: Params of the session.run agent tool (design §4.1): run a command in a session — the agent's lane — through the same submit path a person uses (the renderer's ordinary orchestration: block, ledger entry, attempt, output artifact, all minted at submit). The backend never writes to the PTY (design §2.1 — rejected). The session the tool may run in is bounded by the grant's session scopes, enforced by the narrowed capability (ADR-0028 decision 4); the window contract of the return (design §4.4) is the tool's return contract, not a parameter. The model is untrusted input and gets the same check the renderer's parameters get — additionalProperties: false plus an explicit required list.

sessionId.description: The session (the lane) the command runs in, inside the grant's session scopes.

command.description: The command to submit, exactly as a person would type it.

result.title: SessionRunResult
result.description: What session.run hands back to whoever asked for it — the model under a declared call. The command's output is `text`; there is no `output` and no `stdout` (a live model guessed both). The window contract of design §4.4 is stated here rather than in the params: the renderer clamps a long output and says which span it actually returned, so a truncation is visible instead of silent.

sessionId.description: The session the command ran in.

entryId.description: The ledger entry the command was recorded as. Empty when the store wrote no row (history off), which is an honest answer and not an error.

exitCode.description: The process exit status, or null when the block has none.

status.description: The block's frozen status vocabulary. `entered` means the command was submitted to a program that owns the terminal rather than run to completion.

total.description: Total lines of output the block holds.

start.description: First line of the window that was asked for, counting from 0.

end.description: One past the last line of the window that was asked for.

window.description: The span asked for: the whole output.

start.description: First line of the window actually returned, counting from 0.

end.description: One past the last line of the window actually returned.

returned.description: The span actually returned. Narrower than `window` when the output was clamped; `total` says how much more there is.

truncated.description: True when the returned text was shortened by the declaration's byte bound.

dropped.description: Output bytes omitted from the returned text.

remaining.description: Output bytes still omitted from this response.

text.description: The output itself, over the returned span.
